svg.text: The payment pipeline — one charge across a crash
order 4: crash after the charge, seen-set lost, key survives → charged 6
2 // Two of an event's five fields are CLOCKS, which ch01 established:
3 // et = event time, when it happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // v = the value being summed (also, here, the amount to charge)
5 type Event { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 events, in PROCESSING order (tools/stream_seed.js).
7 // EVENTS[4] = (id 4, key "a", et 245, pt 246, v 6) <- the order this chapter charges
8 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
9 // primitive: WIN — the window width, in seconds of event time. WIN = 120
10 // primitive: CHK — the index whose state was checkpointed before the crash. CHK = 4
11 // primitive: TOTAL — the dataset's true total. TOTAL = 45
12 // primitive: winOf(et) — the START of the window holding et.
14 // primitive: append(xs, x) — xs with x added at the end. append([1], 2) = [1,2]
15 // primitive: contains(xs, x) — is x in xs? contains([1,2], 2) = true
20 // primitive: ORDER — the record being charged. ORDER = EVENTS[4], amount 6
21 // primitive: OFFSET0 — the committed offset before the crash. OFFSET0 = 4
23 // function: charge(proc, key, amount) — the external call; the processor dedups.
32 // function: sinkWrite(proc, pipe, e) — the last stage: dedup, then charge.
33 // sinkWrite(proc, pipe, ORDER) charges 6 the first time, and nothing after
41 // function: crash(pipe) — what the pipeline LOSES: its in-memory seen-set. The
42 // committed offset survives; everything else does not.
48 // function: run(useKey) — charge the order, crash before committing, replay.
54 proc = sinkWrite(proc, pipe, ORDER) // pass 1: charges
57 proc = sinkWrite(proc, pipe, ORDER) // pass 2: the replay
61 // function: main() — THE CALLER: with the key, and without it.
Step 2/0 — the crash takes the seen-set and leaves the offset
`seen` becomes `[]` while `offset` stays 4. That asymmetry is the whole scenario: the offset was durable and the dedup set was in memory, so the replay will
re-read record 4 AND the shuffle will think it is new. The dedup guard is gone exactly when it is needed.
